terminal.emulator: direct PTY with probe-owned loopback HTTP/SSE tool-call fixture

reference.capture: Hades debug binary with isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME and explicit loopback provider configuration

normalization: The binary path, synthetic HOME/HERMES_HOME, PTY path, timestamps, session identifiers, prompt text, assistant text, tool arguments, and raw ANSI redraw stream are omitted or represented by stable markers, lengths, and SHA-256 digests.

The local HTTP server binds only to 127.0.0.1 and records method/path, authorization presence, body keys, model, stream flag, message roles, tool presence, and per-chunk digest boundaries; prompt and argument payloads are never persisted.
The response is reduced to the text/event-stream content type, the fragment count, per-fragment lengths/digests, the joined-argument length/digest, and the finish_reason marker.
No tool is executed, approved, or forwarded: the fixture records executed=false, approved=false, one chat request, zero follow-up chat requests, and zero tool-response requests.
Hades does not yet advertise the Hermes 31-tool inventory (tools_present=false); this fixture covers parsing of a tool-call response, not tool registration or execution.

steps.precondition: Fresh Hades 120x40 PTY with HADES_PROVIDER_BASE_URL set to the probe-owned loopback endpoint and no API key.

visible_state.cleanup: Ctrl+C exited cleanly with alternate screen and termios restored

unknowns: Tool approval, execution, results, retries, malformed/truncated argument handling, multiple tool calls per turn, tool registration/advertising, and follow-up chat requests after a tool-call completion remain unimplemented and unobserved in Hades.

Hermes' post-[DONE] transition (overlay presentation, transcript persistence, tool.start, clarify invocation, follow-up request, retries, and failures) remains unknown per OBS-0110 and is not reproduced in Hades.
